response.headline: Hills between you and the nearest masts are the likely cause [terrain_blocking][los_ee][los_o2][los_three][los_vodafone][network_comparison].

causes.explanation: Terrain rises above the direct line to every operator's nearest site, with no operator having a clear line of sight [los_ee][los_o2][los_three][los_vodafone][network_comparison]; antenna heights are assumed, so the exact margin is uncertain.

The nearest identified mast is 3.8 km away [nearest_site][los_vodafone]; O2's nearest approximate site is 5.7 km away [los_o2]; operators are inferred from crowd-sourced data [nearest_site][los_vodafone][los_o2].
A Met Office yellow wind warning covers the district and gusts may reach 81.4 km/h [weather][met_office_warnings], but this only explains current or recent degradation and is weak sample evidence.
No speed tests exist in this cell or within 1 km [speed_cell][speed_1km], and nearby neighbour data are sparse [speed_neighbours], so the exact point-level cause cannot be confirmed.

actions.text: Try O2 first, as it has the least obstructed line of sight to an identified site [network_comparison][los_o2].
Use Wi-Fi calling indoors if your phone and network support it.
Check your address on Ofcom’s mobile coverage checker: https://www.ofcom.org.uk/mobile-coverage-checker
Emergency calls work on any available network.

response.best_network: O2 is ranked first because it has the least obstructed line of sight, though its site is farther away [network_comparison][los_o2]. EE, Three and Vodafone have closer identified sites but steeper terrain blocking [los_ee][los_three][los_vodafone]. All operators are inferred from crowd-sourced data, so confidence is low [los_ee][los_o2][los_three][los_vodafone][nearest_site].
limitations: Sites are approximate and antenna heights are assumed; Ofcom figures are area-level, not exact for this address.
Causes are inferred from public data, not confirmed: operators' network data is not public.
Ookla speeds are quarterly aggregates with no time-of-day detail; congestion can only be inferred.
No address-level Ofcom coverage; Ofcom figures are for the whole constituency and are predictions.
Mast sites are approximate (crowd-sourced OpenCelliD, OpenStreetMap, Ofcom's licence register) and incomplete, so 'no sites found' is weak evidence.
Line of sight uses a surface model (trees and buildings included) and mostly assumed antenna heights; blocked means a weaker signal, not no signal.
